original_question: Does there exist a field whose Brauer group is isomorphic to Z/7Z?
target_in_paper: Section 11.D, unnumbered question immediately after Conjecture 11.6: Does there exist a field with Brauer group Z/3Z?
correct_elements: Your draft has the right basic shape: it asks for the existence of a field with a prescribed Brauer group, and it focuses on a finite cyclic group, which is exactly the type of question discussed in Section 11.D.
missing_details: The paper’s actual singled-out open case is Z/3Z, not Z/7Z.
The field should be named explicitly, say F, and the group should be written as Br(F).
The isomorphism should be understood as an isomorphism of abelian groups.
To make the question stand alone, 'Brauer group' should mean the classical Brauer group of Brauer classes of central simple F-algebras.
Paper-faithful context is that this is the smallest open case arising from Problem 11.5 and the Brumer-Rosen Conjecture 11.6, not an arbitrary prime-order variant.
No characteristic or roots-of-unity hypothesis belongs to the question itself; those appear only in the related discussion via Problem 3.2.
refined_question: Does there exist a field F such that its Brauer group Br(F), i.e. the Brauer group of Brauer classes of central simple F-algebras over F, is isomorphic as an abelian group to Z/3Z?
justification: The closest paper-faithful target is not the broader Problem 11.5 ('for which n does Br(F) ≅ Z/nZ occur?') but the specific unnumbered question the authors explicitly isolate right after Conjecture 11.6. Your draft is already a one-instance existence question about a finite cyclic Brauer group, so the nearest formulation in the paper is the highlighted smallest open case 'Does there exist a field with Brauer group Z/3Z?'. The surrounding context in Section 11.D explains why this special case is singled out: it is the smallest open case under the Brumer-Rosen framework, and the authors note that it would be settled by a positive answer to Problem 3.2. Hence the main repair needed is replacing 7 by 3 and making Br(F) explicit.

citations.label: unnumbered sentence after Conjecture 11.6 ('The smallest open case is ... Does there exist a field with Brauer group Z/3Z?')
